results.prompt: Make a mono green storm deck in Premodern.
results.text:
I can't build a mono green storm deck from what's legal here. Storm isn't a strategy in the last 30 days of Premodern results, and I found no green storm payoff.

- **Storm payoffs:** Mind's Desire, Tendrils of Agony, Mystical Tutor, Gitaxian Probe, and Brainstorm are all illegal in this format. Dragonstorm is legal but red, and it needs a Dragon in your library.
- **Green enablers:** Birds of Paradise (legal, 329 decks), Llanowar Elves (140), Fyndhorn Elves (128), Wild Growth (588), and Rampant Growth (3) are all legal. Without a payoff, though, they only ramp.
- **Storm count:** Storm needs a large spell count. Green has no cheap spells that build it, so the deck would be a ramp pile with no finisher.

Two ways forward:

1. **Mono green ramp brew.** Build around the legal elves and Wild Growth, then add green creatures that win on their own. I would label it a brew, since no storm or ramp list like this shows up in results.
2. **Green-red storm splash.** Use red for storm-adjacent cards like Dragonstorm, then check the Dragon count before committing. This departs from mono green.

Which do you want? I'll run the card checks and submit the list once you choose.

results.prompt: Make a Legacy deck that wins on turn 1 every game.
results.text:
No Legacy deck wins on turn 1 every game. On the play, a turn-1 kill needs 20 damage or 20 life lost before you have a board. No 60-card list does that against an opposing hand that can answer it, and the field has no deck that comes close.

Here is what the current field offers if you want the fastest realistic clock:

- **Ocelot Aggro** (Tier A, 9.1% meta share, 55 league trophies). The lowest-curve creature deck in the top tier.
- **Doomsday** (Tier A, 5.7%, 37 trophies). Combo that can win as early as turn 1 or 2 when the setup comes off the top, but it fails when it doesn't.
- **Sneak and Show** (Tier B, 3.7%). Fast reanimation-style threat deployment, but only 7 league trophies.

Doomsday is the closest to "usually turn 1 or 2" when it works, and it is also the one that most often does nothing. Ocelot Aggro is the more consistent fast deck.

Tell me which target you want:
1. **Fastest consistent clock.** I build an Ocelot Aggro list from real winning lists and check it against the field.
2. **Highest-variance early kill.** I build a Doomsday list and show how often the setup fails.
3. **A brew.** Give me the cards you want included and I will check legality and build around them. Brews have not shown up in results unless the cards are already in the field.

**Why this shell:** Kiln Fiend gets +3/+0 for each instant or sorcery you cast. The Rally core is 28 instants and sorceries, so the deck has enough triggers to matter.

**Main (60):**
- 4 Kiln Fiend (not in shell results, brew)
- 4 Burning-Tree Emissary (100% of Rally lists)
- 4 Voldaren Epicure (100%)
- 2 Clockwork Percussionist (100%, cut from 4 to fit 18 lands)
- 4 Lightning Bolt (100%)
- 4 Chain Lightning (61%)
- 4 Galvanic Blast (100%)
- 4 Reckless Impulse (88%)
- 4 Wrenn's Resolve (40%, flex in the shell)
- 4 Cast into the Fire (listed as 98% in Rally sideboards, moved to main here as an instant that also clears small blockers)
- 4 Rally at the Hornburg (100%)
- 14 Mountain, 4 Great Furnace

**Sideboard:** 3 Red Elemental Blast, 3 Pyroblast, 2 End the Festivities. These follow the Rally sideboard average. No matchup is named, so I did not tune them.

**Notes:**
- Eighteen lands is a deliberate choice. Burning-Tree and Reckless Impulse give some card flow, but the deck still needs lands for the 4-mana Percussionist and the spell-heavy hand.
- Kiln Fiend's power depends on casting spells before combat. Expect it to be weakest when the hand is all creatures.
- Brew status: the Kiln Fiend slots have no results behind them. Test before relying on the 4-copy count.

results.prompt: Build me a Premodern Dream Halls deck that doesn't win with storm.
results.text:
The list is saved as a Dimir Dream Halls brew. It is not a stock list. None of the five Dream Halls lists in the last 30 days has a non-storm finisher.

**What I changed from the field lists**
- Cut Brain Freeze and Rush of Knowledge, the storm-count and card-draw finishers in both reference lists.
- Cut Lotus Petal, Cunning Wish, Orim's Chant, and Circular Logic. None of them is a finisher, but they are the storm-adjacent core of the Challenge 16 lists.
- Added Psychatog (4) as the creature payload. Show and Tell (2) puts it into play.
- Kept the blue control core: Counterspell (4), Arcane Denial (3), Opportunity, Meditate, Intuition, Frantic Search, and Dream Halls (4).

**Main 60 (18 lands, 42 spells)**
- Lands: 7 Island, 4 Swamp, 3 Saprazzan Skerry, 4 Ancient Tomb
- Win conditions: 4 Psychatog, 2 Show and Tell
- Cost reducer: 4 Dream Halls
- Interaction: 4 Counterspell, 3 Arcane Denial, 2 Chain of Vapor
- Card selection: 4 Opportunity, 4 Meditate, 3 Intuition, 4 Frantic Search, 2 Sleight of Hand, 2 Flash of Insight, 3 Opt, 1 Deep Analysis

**Sideboard:** 3 Defense Grid, 2 Blue Elemental Blast, 2 Annul, 2 Hydroblast.

**Weaknesses to know**
- This is a brew. Psychatog, Show and Tell, and Dream Halls have not appeared together in any reference list I pulled.
- Psychatog is the only black creature. Dream Halls can only make it free by discarding another black card, and the only other black cards are more Psychatogs. Most games it will be cast for {1}{U}{B} or put in by Show and Tell.
- Black sources are thin: 4 Swamp and 3 Skerry, with Tomb adding colorless mana only. Expect color trouble.
- The legal creature pool is small. Mulldrifter, Phyrexian Metamorph, Platinum Angel, and Venser are not legal in this format.
- Show and Tell adds only two payloads. Expect slow wins when it misses.

results.prompt: Build a deck that best utilizes Peter Parker's Camera.
results.text:
**Peter Parker's Camera: Esper Blink brew**

Camera has not shown up in recent Modern results. This list is a brew. It uses the stock Esper Blink shell, which is in 194 recent lists, and adds Camera in place of two slots.

The Camera costs {2}, taps, and removes a film counter to copy a target activated or triggered ability you control. Blink gives it the most targets:

- **Solitude** (99% adoption, 4 copies): copying the ETB exile removes a second creature.
- **Flickerwisp** (66%, 3 copies): copying the ETB flicker repeats the blink.
- **Overlord of the Balemurk** (67%, 4 copies): copying its ETB or attack trigger mills again and returns another creature or planeswalker.
- **Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd** (100%, 4 copies): copying its attack trigger repeats the exile on an attacker.

**Changes from the 1st-place Blink list (Modern Challenge 64, 9-1 variant):**
- Out: 1 Consign to Memory (69% adoption), 1 Witch Enchanter (73%).
- In: 2 Peter Parker's Camera.

**Main (60):**
- 1 Boggart Trawler
- 3 Emperor of Bones
- 3 Flickerwisp
- 4 Overlord of the Balemurk
- 4 Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd
- 4 Quantum Riddler

- 4 Flooded Strand, 2 Godless Shrine, 1 Hallowed Fountain, 4 Marsh Flats, 1 Meticulous Archive, 2 Plains, 1 Polluted Delta, 1 Shadowy Backstreet, 1 Swamp, 1 Undercity Sewers, 1 Watery Grave

**Sideboard (15):** Ashiok, Dream Render; 3 Break the Ice; Clarion Conqueror; 3 Consign to Memory; 2 High Noon; 2 Mystical Dispute; 3 Wrath of the Skies. This is the field's usual Blink board.

The deck is validated and legal. Camera has no results data, so its value is untested. Take it to a matchup and I can check hate cards against the preview.

results.text:
Proposed deck is accepted: **5-color Aluren**, the weirdest list in the current field that still has results.

**Why this one:** Aluren is unranked in the tier list (8 appearances, 2 league trophies), but the reference 5-0 League list (otaba, Premodern League, 2026-10-04) is the same shape as the one I submitted. The Challenge 16 list (ScreenwriterNY, 2-2, 20th place) runs a blue-based version with Sylvan Library and Daze.

**Core engine:**
- Aluren: 4 copies, in 10 of 10 recent decks.
- Survival of the Fittest: 4 copies, in 5 of 10 decks. Used to dig for Aluren.
- Man-o'-War and Raven Familiar: 4 each, both in 10 of 10 decks. Bounce and blockers.
- Cavern Harpy: 4 copies, in 10 of 10 decks.
- Birds of Paradise (3), Wall of Blossoms (2), Wall of Roots (2): mana and early bodies.
- Spike Feeder (2): in 7 of 10 decks.

**Mana:** 23 lands across all five colors (City of Brass, Gemstone Mine, Havenwood Battleground, Llanowar Wastes, Reflecting Pool, Yavimaya Coast, plus basics). This is a fixing-heavy build, so the land count matters.

**Main deck:** 3 Cabal Therapy. The 5-0 list ran it in the main, and it appears in 5 of 10 decks overall.

**Sideboard (15):**
- 3 Naturalize (in 9 of 10 decks)
- 4 Tormod's Crypt (6 of 10)
- 3 Xantid Swarm (10 of 10)
- 2 Tsabo's Web (6 of 10)
- 2 Compost (8 of 10)

I did not run a matchup preview, since you did not name an opponent. If you tell me what you expect to face, I can build a board for it.
